note: High-water mark for the C3/C4/C5 mechanical-proof migration. Until 2026-08-03 the ONLY check on C3 (durable state survives process restart), C4 (tamper-evidence / integrity chain) and C5 (fail-safe reporting: unavailable rather than a plausible zero) was that the written verdict was at least 8 characters long. All 46 greens fail the real bar today, 132 of 135 gaps being 'no referent named at all', so enforcing it outright would demote the entire green ledger at a stroke -- an operator decision, not a gate decision. This number may only go DOWN. Lower it as organs earn real proofs; never raise it to make a failing gate pass. When it reaches 0, --enforce-condition-proofs becomes the permanent default and this file can be deleted. CORRECTION 2026-08-05: the number is unchanged at 46, but what it MEASURES was broken until now. tests/test_condition_proof_ratchet.py asked the predicate with results={} intending 'did this verdict name a referent at all', and the predicate instead scored every named-but-unexecuted proof as a failure. Because C5 has no N/A-BY-DESIGN clause, every organ must cite a test and every citation scored 'did not execute', so no organ could EVER be gap-free: the live gap was identically the green count and the assertion reduced to 'greens <= 46'. It was a green-count cap, passing only by the coincidence that 46 == 46, and no amount of proof work could move it. The measurement now uses require_execution=False and asks the naming question it always claimed to. The count is coincidentally identical because every green still lacks a referent somewhere -- C5 is unnamed on all 46 -- but the number can now actually fall, and a well-proven new green no longer consumes budget.

how_to_discharge.C3: name a test as 'tests/foo.py::test_bar' in the C3 verdict (it must run and pass in the gate's own run), or discharge with 'N/A-BY-DESIGN - path::symbol' whose cite resolves
how_to_discharge.C4: same as C3 -- both are defined as '... (or N/A-BY-DESIGN with cite)'
how_to_discharge.C5: must be positively proven with a named test; C5's definition carries no N/A-BY-DESIGN clause, and inventing one would be the exact failure mode this gate exists to catch
